blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Singapore have agreed to update their nearly 50-year-old double taxation agreement to align their tax systems with economic and international changes. The Department of Finance (DOF) announced that negotiators reached the agreement after four days of talks held in Singapore from Sept. 22 to 25. READ: Gov’t renegotiating 3 double tax treaties, pursuing 7 new pacts However, the updated provisions have not yet been made public because the agreement still requires presidential ratification. “The Philippines is committed to strengthening tax cooperation across the region.
